question.problem:
The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ),$ given by 

$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨6\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____},\,6\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

parametrizes one sheet of the hyperboloid of two sheets defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}=-36.$ By expressing the equation of the hyperboloid in cylindrical polar coordinates, determine the second component of $f.$
question.worked_solution:
If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(x,y,z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

Substituting this into our equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2} & =-36 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}-{z}^{2} & =-36 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )-{z}^{2} & =-36 \\ {r}^{2}-{z}^{2} & =-36 \\ {z}^{2}-{r}^{2} & =36\end{aligned}
$$

Here, the hyperbola ${z}^{2}-{r}^{2}=36$ represents the intersection of our hyperboloid with the plane that passes through the $z$-axis and makes the angle of $\theta $ with the positive $x$-axis. Using the hint, a parametrization of such hyperbola can be given as

$$
⟨z,r⟩=⟨6\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ,\,6\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ⟩,\,ϕ\in R.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩ \\  & =⟨(6\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,(6\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,6\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨6\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,6\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,6\operatorname{cosh}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in R.$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $6\operatorname{sinh}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
